title: CHAPTER SIXTEEN. On the will of God; definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): ye learned Molina rightly notes that same it stands as not properly attributed to God in this sense, because reason also does not properly belong to God — but when it stands as defined as rational appetite. Ephesians 1:11. Matthew 20:15; Psalm 115:3; James 1:18; Romans 9:18; Daniel 4:17; both ye perfection belonging toward God's essence plus intellect, plus Scripture, plus ye consent belonging toward men abundantly confirm — Jonah 1:14; — that will stands as rightly attributed to God. will stands as that same life belonging toward His by means belonging toward that same which God stands as borne toward a known good. This stands as God's image: On ye will belonging toward God. CHAPTER SIXTEEN.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN. On the will of God.

This is God's image: will is that life of His by which God is borne toward a known good. That will is rightly attributed to God, both the perfection of God's essence and intellect, and Scripture, and the consent of men abundantly confirm — Jonah 1:14; Daniel 4:17; Romans 9:18; James 1:18; Psalm 115:3; Matthew 20:15; Ephesians 1:11.
But when it is defined as rational appetite, the learned Molina rightly notes that it is not properly attributed to God in this sense, because reason also does not properly belong to God.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMSEXTUM, De voluntate Dei. Haec Dei imago est: voluntas est illius vita, qua Deus in bonum cognitum fertur. Voluntatem Deo recte tribui tum essentiae et intellectus Dei perfectio, tum Scriptura, hominumque consensus abunde confirmant — Jonae I.14; Dan. IV.17; Rom. IX.18; Jac. I.18; Psal. CXV.3; Matth. XX.15; Ephes. I.11. Cum autem definitur orexis noera, appetitus rationalis, Deo proprie hoc sensu non tribui recte notat CL. P. Molinaeus, quia nec ratio proprie Deo competit.
